title: New traffic lights coming to Rainsville intersection - NewsBreak
text: RAINSVILLE, Ala. (WHNT) — The mayor of Rainsville says the city is getting a new set of traffic lights for an intersection that many consider dangerous. According to Mayor Rodger Lingerfelt, the intersection of Highway 35 and Marshall Road has been the cause of many accidents in the city. “It’s extremely dangerous. A lot of cars coming through there. They’re going through at a good pace through that red light,” Lingerfelt said. “We have quite a few accidents at that red light. So, yes, it is definitely a safety hazard.” He said the city has received a commitment from the State to upgrade the existing traffic lights to include a left-turn signal, making it easier and safer for people to make left turns. An employee at a nearby gas station said she has witnessed several accidents and close calls at the intersection. She’s hopeful that the new lights will make it safer for drivers to pass through. The upgrades will cost $36,000 and will take about two months to complete. Lingerfelt said the project is scheduled to start in the next few weeks. For the latest news, weather, sports, and streaming video, head to WHNT.com.
